l60_score.title: L60 Long-Term Position Score
l60_score.summary: Measures intermediate-to-long-term trend strength and durability over a rolling 60-day horizon, focusing on core moving average alignments.
l60_score.origin: Project AETHER Core Team (Calibration Backtest, 336k obs 2023-2025) + Pattern Discovery calibration (Jul 2026). LT Trend and Industry Strength contrarian weights removed after retrospective analysis showed they systematically excluded 95% and 81% of 60-day winners.
l60_score.body:
Measures intermediate-to-long-term trend quality over a 60-day horizon. Note: the L60 contrarian logic for LT Trend and Industry Strength was removed in July 2026 after Pattern Discovery analysis across 3 historical replay dates showed these penalized factors were present in the vast majority of 60-day winners — the opposite of the intended contrarian effect.

Key calibration change (Jul 2026):

  • LT Trend=Strong: was -3.0 → now 0.0. In 95% of L60 missed winners across 3 test dates (Oct 2025, Dec 2025, Mar 2026), the stock had Strong lt_trend. The contrarian assumption ("strong trend = overbought") does not hold for 60-day holds.
  • Industry Strength=Strong: was -1.5 → now 0.0. Present in 81% of L60 missed winners. Sector leadership is a feature for 60-day holds, not a mean-reversion warning.

The contrarian logic was correct for S10 (10-day mean reversion) but incorrect for L60 (60-day trend following). These are now treated as neutral signals in L60.

candlestick_engine.title: Japanese Candlestick Recognition Engine
candlestick_engine.summary: Nets 17 candlestick patterns (12 classical + 5 modern Kaabar formations) over a rolling 5-session window into a [-2, +2] score. Open the card for the full catalogue, each pattern linked to a good explanation online.
candlestick_engine.origin: Munehisa Homma (1700s Japanese rice trading), extended with Daniel Chesler's Hikkake and Sofien Kaabar's modern trend-following patterns (Mastering Financial Pattern Recognition, O'Reilly).
candlestick_engine.body:
Scans the last 5 sessions for 17 candlestick patterns and nets their bullish vs. bearish fires into one score in [-2, +2] ((bulls − bears) / 5 × 2, clamped). Bullish clusters tilt the entry score up; bearish clusters pull it down. Twelve are classical Japanese/Western formations; five are modern trend-following patterns coined by Sofien Kaabar. Each name links to a full explanation:

Classical reversal & continuation
  • • Engulfing — the 2nd body fully engulfs the 1st — strong reversal.
  • • Harami — small body contained inside the prior large body; reversal / pause.
  • • Harami (strict) — stricter Harami — the whole small candle sits inside the prior body.
  • • Doji — open ≈ close; indecision, a reversal hinge between two trend candles.
  • • Star (Morning / Evening) — small gapped middle candle between two opposite bodies; reversal.
  • • Piercing / Dark Cloud — gap then a close back through the midpoint of the prior body; reversal.
  • • Tasuki Gap — gap in the trend, then a partial fill that holds; continuation.
  • • Three Methods (Rising / Falling) — 3 small counter-candles inside a big one, then breakout; continuation.
  • • Hikkake — inside-bar false breakout that traps, then reverses (Daniel Chesler).
  • • Tweezers (Top / Bottom) — back-to-back matching highs or lows; minor reversal.
  • • On-Neck — second close returns exactly to the prior close; continuation.
  • • Stick Sandwich — two same-close candles bracketing an opposite one (Bulkowski stats).
Modern trend-following (Sofien Kaabar)
  • • Bottle — trend candle opening flush with its low/high after a gap; momentum.
  • • Double Trouble — a bar whose range exceeds 2× ATR extending the move.
  • • Quintuplets — five consecutive small same-colour bodies; exhaustion/continuation.
  • • Slingshot — breakout, shallow pullback, then re-break in the trend direction.
  • • H Pattern — doji flanked by two same-direction candles forming an 'H'; continuation.

Detectors live in aether/signals.py; aggregation in aether/patterns.py :: candlestick_score().
config: Patterns scanned (17): Engulfing, Harami (+strict), Doji, Piercing, Star, Tasuki Gap, Three Methods, Hikkake, Tweezers, On-Neck, Stick Sandwich, Bottle, Double Trouble, Quintuplets, Slingshot, H.
Lookback: the last 5 sessions; each pattern counts once if it fires anywhere in the window.
Score: net (bullish - bearish) fires, scaled (raw / 5 x 2) and clamped to [-2, +2].
Small-body threshold: 1% of the recent 5-bar average close (gates Tweezers & Quintuplets).
Double Trouble range gate: bar high-low range > 2x the prior ATR.
Source: aether/signals.py detectors + aether/patterns.py::candlestick_score().

The cap is dynamic: it ramps smoothly from the 20% base toward a per-profile ceiling as a candidate's conviction score (Short10 + Long60) rises, and every buy is additionally clamped to a per-position ceiling so no single name can dominate. digit_sum_numerology.title: Digit-Sum Numerology Factor
digit_sum_numerology.summary: Backtested across 522 symbols × 9+ years. Tests whether the digit-sum of a stock's open/close price predicts same-day or next-day direction. Two variants (integer and full-cents) cover 228 unique symbols with 95%+ confidence signals. Of 473 raw signals, 224 pass the full 4-layer quality validator and are active in scoring. Symbol page shows a Stability column: stable / mixed / sparse / flip.
digit_sum_numerology.origin: Inspired by W.D. Gann's numerology research (1878–1955). Empirically backtested by AETHER across 522 symbols × 9+ years of daily OHLCV data (2014–2026).
digit_sum_numerology.body:
Tests whether the digit-sum of a stock's price predicts short-term direction. Digit-sum collapses any price to a single digit: $247.35 → 2+4+7+3+5=21 → 3.

AETHER runs two variants simultaneously:

  • Integer digit-sum — whole-dollar only ($247 → 4). 162/522 symbols with 95%+ signals.
  • Full-cents digit-sum — includes cents ($247.35 → 3). Adds 106 unique symbols not captured by integer-only.

Two timing modes:

  • Prior-close → next-day: standing factor in S10/L60, computed nightly from OHLCV cache.
  • Today's open → same-day: real-time tiebreaker in _execute_buys() using live open price. Logged as 🔢 [Digit-Sum].

Of 473 signals at 95%+ confidence, only 224 pass all four quality gates and are used in scoring. See the Signal Quality Validator wiki entry for the full filter pipeline.

The Symbol detail modal shows a digit table with a Stability column: stable / mixed / sparse / flip / stale.
config: Integer digit-sum OPEN→same-day: real-time only, applied in _execute_buys() at buy time
Integer digit-sum CLOSE→next-day: standing factor, S10 weight ±1.0, L60 weight ±0.5
Full-cents digit-sum: same two modes, combined with integer (averaged when both fire)
Activation gate: |z|≥2.0 (95%+ confidence), N≥50 per bucket
Score scale: z/3.0 capped at ±1.0 per variant; averaged when both fire
Quality filter: temporal + flip + sparse checks — 473 raw → 224 active signals
Monthly refresh: python scripts/backtesting/digit_sum_study.py + digit_sum_full_study.py

pattern_discovery.title: Pattern Discovery Agent — Missed Winners Retrospective
pattern_discovery.summary: Weekly self-improvement loop: replay a past date, find the top 10 actual winners, diagnose why each was missed, and extract candidate new scoring factors. Two-layer design — a Python computation engine reconstructs 475 symbol scores from the Chaikin cache in ~14s (parallelized), followed by an LLM agent that reasons about why patterns exist and names them. First finding (Jul 2026): lt_trend=Strong penalized -3.0 in L60 appeared in 95% of missed 60-day winners across 3 dates — weight corrected to 0. Run from the System page or via /pattern-discover.
pattern_discovery.origin: AETHER Internal R&D (July 2026). Inspired by W.D. Gann's retrospective analysis approach and Amy Edmondson's Right Kind of Wrong — learning from intelligent failures.
pattern_discovery.body:
A self-improving learning loop that finds stocks the system missed, diagnoses why it missed them, and extracts candidate new scoring factors.

How it works (run weekly on Saturdays):

  1. Historical replay — reconstructs every symbol's AETHER scores as they were on a past date (reads from the Chaikin per-symbol cache, no live API needed).
  2. Forward returns — computes actual 10-day (S10) and 60-day (L60) returns from OHLCV for all symbols.
  3. Classify winners — ranks actual winners; marks each as bought (system selected it), missed (system rejected it despite being in universe), or not in universe.
  4. Diagnose misses — for each missed winner records the exact filter that rejected it (score < threshold, wrong PGR, setup=False) and which factor was most anomalous vs the universe.
  5. Extract patterns — two types: (a) missed-winner patterns: factor combos present in missed winners but penalized in the model; (b) false-positive guards: signals common in stocks the system bought that then lost.
  6. Validate — rolls candidate patterns across 16 historical dates. Only patterns with |z|≥2.0 and N≥30 are promoted to the scoring backlog.

First finding (Jul 2026): lt_trend=Strong appeared in 95% of L60 missed winners across 3 dates. The -3.0 contrarian penalty was excluding exactly the stocks that performed best over 60 days. Weight updated: Strong → 0 (was -3.0) in L60.

Run from the System page, or invoke the /pattern-discover skill for full LLM reasoning over the results.
config: Replay date: target ~3-4 weeks back so both 10d and 60d windows have settled OHLCV data
Constraint: replay date ≤ 2026-04-04 for 10d window, ≤ 2026-02-24 for 60d window
Reconstruction: reads Data/Symbol/{sym}/{sym}_{date}.json Chaikin cache (no live session needed)
Thresholds: score ≥ 9.5 AND pgr ∈ {Bu, Bu+} AND setup=True to qualify as 'bought'
Validation: 16 sampled dates across 9-month range, |z|≥2.0 + N≥30 for promotion
Output: Data/pattern_discovery_{DATE}.json — machine-readable for the /pattern-discover skill
Weekly cadence: run same date each week; pattern recurring in 3+ weeks = strong validation signal

signal_quality_validator.title: Signal Quality Validator — 4-Layer Filter Pipeline
signal_quality_validator.summary: 4-layer filter pipeline that rejects statistical signals concentrated in the wrong time period, self-contradicting across eras, or from price regimes no longer relevant. Checks: (1) |z|≥2.0 significance, (2) temporal persistence across 6 rolling 2-year windows, (3) no direction flip between eras, (4) adequate coverage at current price level. Reusable framework for all future experimental factors.
signal_quality_validator.origin: AETHER Internal R&D — discovered during temporal distribution audit of digit-sum signals (July 2026).
signal_quality_validator.body:
Before any statistical signal enters the scoring engine, AETHER runs it through a 4-layer quality filter to reject noise masquerading as signal.

The problem discovered: a signal can show z=+2.5 overall yet be completely unreliable — if it fired 700 times when a stock was at $15 and only 30 times at today's $200, or if it was bullish in 2016 and bearish in 2022.

The 4 filters applied in sequence:

  1. Statistical significance — |z| ≥ 2.0 (95%+ confidence) with N ≥ 50 days per bucket. Eliminates weak correlations.
  2. Temporal consistency — Signal is tested across 6 rolling 2-year windows (2014–2026). Must fire in same direction in ≥ 2 windows to be kept; ≥ 4 windows = "stable". Rejects historically-concentrated signals.
  3. Direction stability (has_flip) — If the signal is bullish in some windows and bearish in others, it is rejected. A self-contradicting signal has no predictive value regardless of overall z-score.
  4. Coverage adequacy (is_sparse) — The digit must appear in ≥ 3 of 6 windows (coverage ≥ 50%). Low coverage means the digit barely exists at the stock's current price level — the signal has no recent history to validate.

Result for digit-sum: 473 signals at 95%+ → 224 pass all four gates (53% rejection rate). Each rejected signal is still displayed in the Symbol modal Stability column so you can see exactly why it was downgraded.

This pipeline is reusable — future experimental factors (Gann levels, gap persistence, round-number proximity) will run through the same 4-layer validator before entering the score.
config: Layer 1 — Statistical: |z| ≥ 2.0, N ≥ 50 per bucket
Layer 2 — Temporal: fires in same direction in ≥ 2 of 6 rolling 2-year windows
Layer 3 — Direction: no flip (bullish in some windows, bearish in others) → rejected
Layer 4 — Coverage: digit appears in ≥ 3/6 windows (≥ 50% coverage) → sparse = rejected
Symbol modal Stability badge: stable (4+ windows) | mixed (2-3) | flip | sparse | stale
Scoring engine only loads signals passing layers 2+3+4 — stale/flip/sparse excluded
473 raw digit-sum signals → 224 active after all filters (53% rejection rate)

rbr.title: Rubber-Band Reversal (RBR) — Overreaction Pullback + Fast Recovery
rbr.summary: A positively-signed bullish factor: a big, fast overreaction drawdown (Leg 1) followed by a confirmed higher-low green reversal bar in the upper half of its range (Leg 2). Pure price/volume, no look-ahead — the trough must already be in before the recovery bar scores. The tradeable event is the confirmed recovery bar, not the gap. Backtested on 25+ yr of OHLCV; only the reliable no-gap pocket scores, while the higher-variance earnings-gap cohort is watch-only (RBR↑(gap,watch)). Anchored on INTC's Jul-2026 snap-back.
rbr.origin: AETHER Internal R&D (Aug 2026 lab), anchored on INTC's Jul-2026 earnings gap. Formalizes the AI-age machine/headline-driven overshoot-then-V-recover tape.
rbr.body: A positively-signed BULLISH factor: a big, fast overreaction drawdown (Leg 1) followed by a CONFIRMED higher-low green reversal bar sitting in the upper half of its range (Leg 2). Pure price/volume, no look-ahead — the trough must already be in before the recovery bar scores. The tradeable event is the confirmed recovery bar, not the gap (catching INTC's knife on day one ate another -11% before the bounce). Fed to short_score (+0.5) / long_score (+0.25) through the dedicated vrecovery_score field, never the negated contrarian chart path.
config: Leg 1 depth: <= -10% overreaction floor; <= -15% = the validated deep pocket
Leg 1 speed: trough within <= 8 bars; <= 5 bars = the fast pocket
Leg 2: higher low + green close + close in upper half of range (range_pos >= 0.50)
+2.0 validated no-gap pocket (deep + fast + strong close)
+1.25 near-fast no-gap recovery (one bar outside the pocket)
+1.0 milder confirmed recovery
0.0 earnings-GAP cohort — WATCH-ONLY (tag RBR↑(gap,watch)): win ~0.52, never cleared its own gate, so it is surfaced to watch but carries no buy weight
Shared Leg-1 geometry: patterns.rbr_leg1(); live monitor: scripts/monitoring/rbr_watch.py; parameter sweep recalibrated MONTHLY

profit_lock.title: AETHER Profit-Lock (Trailing Stop Ratchet)
profit_lock.origin: Project AETHER Loss-Minimization core, extending Peter Lynch's 'let winners run' with a mechanical breakeven ratchet (plans/trailing-stop-adjuster.md).
profit_lock.summary: Ratchets the trailing stop upward as a position rallies. Once unrealized profit exceeds 1.0× ATR the stop begins climbing behind price; past 1.5× ATR it locks the stop to the cost basis — a breakeven lock that makes the trade risk-free early in the trend.
profit_lock.body: Dynamically tightens the stop-loss floor upward as an open position moves into profit, so gains are progressively protected without capping the upside. Two rungs, both measured in ATR of unrealized profit above the cost basis: at > 1.0× ATR the stop ratchets up to trail price, and at > 1.5× ATR it jumps to the cost basis (breakeven), so the position can no longer close red. Structural-Scarcity holdings use a tighter 1.5× ATR multiplier; standard satellites use the profile ATR multiplier (2.5×). The stop is only ever moved up, never down.
config: Ratchet rung: unrealized profit > 1.0x ATR -> stop trails up behind price
Breakeven lock: unrealized profit > 1.5x ATR -> stop floor bumped to cost basis
ATR multiplier: 1.5x for Scarcity-core names, else the profile ATR multiplier (2.5x)
Monotonic: the stop is only raised, never lowered
Source: ai_portfolio_game.py profit-lock ratchet (see plans/trailing-stop-adjuster.md)

zero_cash_drag.title: Zero-Cash Drag Autopilot & Fractional Sizing
zero_cash_drag.origin: Project AETHER capital-efficiency core; regime read from get_market_regime() (SPY Long60).
zero_cash_drag.summary: Drops the cash buffer to 0.0% in the AGGRESSIVE market regime (SPY L60 > 2) to fully deploy capital when the broad trend is strong. Pairs with 3-decimal fractional share sizing (e.g. 1.458 shares) on S&P 100 blue chips and core ETFs (DIA, SPY, QQQ, IWM) so almost no cash sits idle.
zero_cash_drag.body: Eliminates the drag of uninvested cash when the market regime justifies it. When get_market_regime() returns AGGRESSIVE — the strong-bull state defined by SPY Long60 > 2 — the required cash buffer is dropped to 0%, so the autopilot can deploy fully. To spend the last sliver of cash instead of leaving a stub, sizing supports fractional shares to 3 decimals (values like 1.458 shares) on S&P 100 blue chips and the core ETFs (DIA, SPY, QQQ, IWM). In weaker regimes the profile's normal cushion still applies (Balanced 20%, Defensive 50%) — zero-drag is specifically the AGGRESSIVE-regime behavior, not a blanket setting.
config: Trigger: market regime == AGGRESSIVE (SPY Long60 > 2)
Effect: required cash buffer dropped to 0.0% for full deployment
Fractional sizing: 3-decimal share quantities (e.g. 1.458) on S&P 100 names + DIA/SPY/QQQ/IWM
Non-aggressive regimes retain their normal cash cushion (Balanced 20%, Defensive 50%)
Source: ai_portfolio_game.py regime/cash-buffer logic + aether/instruments.py fractional sizing

momentum_floor.title: Strict Short10 Momentum Floor (S10 ≥ 2.5)
momentum_floor.origin: AETHER backtrack calibration (scripts/backtesting/backtrack_rules.py) — a single-filter entry gate proven on historical replay.
momentum_floor.summary: Backtest-proven entry filter that strictly blocks buying any setup whose Short-Term entry score (Short10) is < 2.5. Backtracking verifies this single filter avoids ~40% of historically losing trades (including PKX, ETHT, SA), boosting the historical Win Rate from 50.0% to 66.7% and nearly tripling net P&L from +7.75% to +27.88%.
momentum_floor.body: A hard pre-buy gate: on autopilot, any candidate whose Short10 entry score is below 2.5 is rejected outright, regardless of its long-term score or PGR. The threshold was not guessed — backtracking the rule over historical trades showed it filters out roughly 40% of the losers (PKX, ETHT, SA among them) while keeping the winners, lifting the sample win rate from 50.0% to 66.7% and net P&L from +7.75% to +27.88%. It enforces the discipline of never buying weak short-term momentum just because the long-term thesis looks attractive.
config: Gate: reject buy when Short10 < 2.5
Scope: applied on autopilot at buy-selection time
Backtest lift: win rate 50.0% -> 66.7%, net P&L +7.75% -> +27.88%
Source: ai_portfolio_game.py buy loop; evidence scripts/backtesting/backtrack_rules.py

capital_flexibility.title: Dynamic Slot Expansion & Pyramiding
capital_flexibility.origin: Project AETHER capital-efficiency core — anti-cash-drag deployment logic.
capital_flexibility.summary: Automatically expands the maximum position-slot count by one when idle cash exceeds 15% and all slots are already full, so strong markets are not left under-deployed. Complements this with Dynamic Pyramiding — scaling additional cash into existing green winners near their breakout closes.
capital_flexibility.body: Prevents cash drag when the portfolio is fully allocated but still holding idle cash. Dynamic Slot Expansion: when the cash ratio exceeds 15% and every position slot is occupied, the maximum-positions limit is bumped by one so a fresh high-conviction candidate can still be entered rather than leaving cash uninvested. Dynamic Pyramiding: instead of only opening new names, the autopilot can add to existing winning positions trading near their recent peak closes, concentrating capital into what is already working. Both mechanisms remain bounded by the standard per-position and Scarcity-bucket caps — they deploy idle cash, they do not override the allocation ceilings.
config: Slot Expansion: cash ratio > 15% AND all slots full -> max_positions += 1
Dynamic Pyramiding: add idle cash to existing green winners near peak closes
Bounded: still clamped by the per-position ceiling and the Scarcity-core cap
Source: ai_portfolio_game.py slot-expansion + pyramiding blocks
